S035-01.notes: Folding tables, bedsheets, car batteries = improvised; 'makeshift'. Permanent/specialized/luxurious all contradict the details.

S035-02.notes: Contrast with dismissive contemporaries + later confirmation = foresighted ('prescient'). Outdated reverses; arbitrary/deliberate off-target. Arrhenius 1896 doubling-CO2 estimate (~5-6 C) consistent with 'several degrees'.

S035-03.notes: Surprising rail-like network from brainless single cell, then engineers' interest. No theory rejected, no second organism, no rail-system problem. Facts match Tero et al. (Tokyo/oat flakes).

S035-04.notes: Timber scarcity + 'walked' oral tradition + upright rope-rocking replica (2012, Lipo/Hunt, 18 people) => moved upright with ropes. A contradicts quarry; C contradicts tradition's fit; D contradicts timber argument and overclaims.

flags: minor: D (both call conditions >1.2 s vs <1 s with no call) also loosely supports similarity of the two call types; A is clearly better because it directly quantifies the hands-free vs handheld gap that 'nearly as much' requires, but D is a reasonably strong distractor.
S035-05.notes: Conclusion is a comparison of hands-free to handheld; A gives the 0.1 s gap. B and C each address only one call type against baseline. Data internally consistent (0.4, 0.5, 0.1 differences correct).

S035-06.notes: Only C isolates ground vibrations (no airborne sound) and shows a response. A is airborne; B is about frequency, not detection; D irrelevant. Matches O'Connell-Rodwell's Etosha seismic playback work.

S035-07.notes: Goal is purpose; only B states the anti-jamming torpedo-guidance purpose. A=mechanism, C/D=background. Facts accurate (1942 patent, 88 frequencies).

S035-08.notes: 'Most are asteroidal' then a qualifying exception 'a small number come from Mars' -> concessive/contrast 'That said'. Accordingly (causal), For example (Martian ones are not an example of asteroid fragments), Similarly (not parallel) fail. Viking 1976 gas match accurate.

S035-09.notes: List items contain internal commas and items already separated by semicolon (Chile;), so the final separator must be '; and'. Comma would be inconsistent; no punctuation or colon wrong.

S035-10.notes: 'required that every vessel ___' takes the mandative subjunctive base form 'store'. 'stores'/'stored' are indicative; 'storing' leaves no finite verb.
